claims.text: The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy is produced by vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization at 2100°C for 2 h.
Approximately 30% of the Hf sublattice should be replaced with V and Al.
The proposed modified composition is approximately (Hf0.70V0.25Al0.05)MoTaTiZr.
The proposed alloy contains approximately 20–25 at.% V and 5 at.% Al.
Homogenization at 2100°C for 2 h followed by air cooling can produce a homogeneous material without precipitation.
The modified V- and Al-containing alloy will remain a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution.
The modified alloy will avoid formation of brittle intermetallic phases.
The V and Al substitutions will retain sufficient lattice distortion for solid-solution strengthening.
A small Al addition will induce beneficial short-range ordering.
Replacing Hf with lighter V and Al will reduce alloy density.
Vanadium will cause substantial lattice-distortion strengthening in the modified alloy.
Al-induced ordering will impede dislocation motion and contribute to strength.
The combined V and Al mechanisms will preserve high yield strength from room temperature through 1000°C.
The modified alloy will have a density 10–12% below that of baseline HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will retain approximately 90–100% of the baseline room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength near 855 MPa at 1000°C.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr has a density of about 10.21 g/cm³, a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa, and a 1000°C yield strength of about 855 MPa.
The hypothesis is rejected if density reduction is below 10%, room-temperature yield strength is below about 1440 MPa, or 1000°C yield strength is below about 770 MPa.

The modified alloy and baseline control will be prepared under identical processing and compared by density measurement, phase and composition analysis, and tensile tests at room temperature and 1000°C.

contradictions.description: The formula (Hf0.70V0.25Al0.05)MoTaTiZr normalizes to approximately Hf 14 at.%, V 5 at.%, Al 1 at.%, and 20 at.% each Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr—not the stated 20–25 at.% V and 5 at.% Al.

The material is repeatedly called 'as-cast,' but it is also specified as subsequently homogenized at 2100°C for 2 h. As-cast and as-homogenized are distinct material conditions, so the baseline and test state are not defined consistently.
